accepted.question_text: Let C4 denote the 4-cycle, and let f(n; C4) be the number of labeled graphs on n vertices that do not contain C4 as a subgraph. Is it true that f(n; C4) = 2^((1/2 + o(1)) n^(3/2)) as n tends to infinity?
accepted.context_brief: Asymptotic enumeration of labeled C4-free graphs.

evidence.quote: As far as I know f(n; C4) = 2^(1/2 + o(1))n3/2 is still open.

accepted.question_text: Fix a constant c > 0. For a graph on n vertices with cn^2 edges, assume every edge belongs to at least one triangle. Let f(n; c) be the largest integer such that some edge of the graph is contained in at least f(n; c) triangles. Determine f(n; c) as sharply as possible, from above and below, as a function of n and c.
accepted.context_brief: How many triangles must concentrate on one edge in a dense graph?

evidence.quote: Estimate f(n ; c) as well as possible both from above and below.

accepted.question_text: Find the smallest integer k > 1 for which there exists an integer n such that gcd(n, n + k) = 1, but for every integer i with 1 <= i < k one has gcd(n + i, n + k) > 1.
accepted.context_brief: Consecutive integers with prescribed gcd pattern.

evidence.quote: Find the smallest integer k > 1 and an integer n such that gcd(n, n + k) = 1 and gcd(n + i, n + k) > 1 for each i, 1 <= i < k.

accepted.question_text: Let m(4) be the minimum size of a family of 4-element subsets of a set S with the property that every 2-coloring of S makes at least one of those 4-subsets monochromatic. Improve either the lower bound or the upper bound for m(4).
accepted.context_brief: Extremal size of a 4-set family forcing a monochromatic member.

evidence.quote: Can you improve the lower or the upper bound?

accepted.question_text: A graph is called orientably simple if it embeds in the torus T but does not embed in the Klein bottle K. Characterize the orientably simple graphs, without requiring the characterization to be by excluded minors.
accepted.context_brief: Graphs embeddable in the torus but not the Klein bottle.

evidence.quote: A graph G that embeds in T but not K we call orientably simple. The problem is to characterize orientably simple graphs, not necessarily by excluded minors.

accepted.question_text: For almost every graph on n vertices, does there exist a collection of cliques such that each vertex belongs to only o(n) of the chosen cliques while all but o(n^2) edges are covered by those cliques? More sharply, can one achieve a per-vertex bound of order O(n / log n)?
accepted.context_brief: Sparse-incidence clique coverings of almost all graphs.

evidence.quote: Can one find cliques with each vertex in o(n) cliques such that o(n^2) edges are uncovered? The best possible result would be f(n) = O(n/log n).

accepted.question_text: Let f(n) be the maximum graph distance between two triangulations of a fixed n-gon, where two triangulations are adjacent when one is obtained from the other by flipping a single diagonal inside a quadrilateral. Is the upper bound f(n) <= 2n - 10, valid for n >= 8, asymptotically and exactly optimal?
accepted.context_brief: Maximum flip distance between triangulations of an n-gon.

evidence.quote: It is easy to show f(n) < 2n - 10 (for n > 8), which is conjectured optimal.

accepted.question_text: Using threshold graphs instead of cliques, determine the correct extremal behavior of threshold-graph coverings and large threshold subgraphs. In particular: (i) if a graph family has nth member edge-coverable by 2n threshold graphs but requiring 3n threshold graphs for an edge-partition, is that 3n requirement best possible? and (ii) if a graph with 2n vertices and n^2 + 1 edges must contain a threshold subgraph with n(1 + 1/2) edges, what is the correct constant c for which one can force a threshold subgraph with cn edges?
accepted.context_brief: Threshold-graph covering and density extremal questions.

evidence.quote: I have a family of graphs such that the nth graph can be edge-covered by 2n threshold graphs, but requires 3n threshold graphs to edge-partition it. Is this best possible?
We think it need not contain a threshold graph with n(1 + 5/8) edges. What is the correct multiple of n?

accepted.question_text: Let c(n) and b(n) denote, respectively, the numbers of central and bicentral unlabeled trees with n vertices. Does the ratio c(n) / b(n) tend to 1 as n tends to infinity?
accepted.context_brief: Asymptotic ratio of central to bicentral unlabeled trees.

evidence.quote: CONJECTURE: Let c(n) and b(n) be the numbers of central and bicentral unlabeled n-vertex trees, respectively. Then c(n)/b(n) -> 1 as n -> oo.

accepted.question_text: Color the unit interval by k measurable color classes. An m-partition is a partition of the interval into m disjoint subsets, each a finite union of intervals, such that every part captures exactly 1/m of the measure of each color. Let c(m, k) be the smallest number of cuts needed, in the worst case, to produce such an m-partition. Is c(m, k) = (m - 1)k for all m and k?

evidence.quote: REMARK: The conjecture has now been proved by Alon.

accepted.question_text: For a generating set T of the symmetric group S_n, let Gamma(S_n, T) be the Cayley graph with vertex set S_n and edges [g, gt] for g in S_n and t in T. Does there exist an absolute constant c such that for every n and every generating set T of S_n, the diameter of Gamma(S_n, T) is less than n^c?
accepted.context_brief: Polynomial diameter bound for Cayley graphs of symmetric groups.

evidence.quote: Prove (or disprove) that there exists a constant c such that for every n and for every set T of generators of the symmetric group S_n, the diameter of Gamma(S_n, T) is less than n^c.

accepted.question_text: Label the edges of the complete graph K_n bijectively by 1, 2, ..., binom(n, 2). For a labeling lambda, let l(lambda) be the length of the longest simple path whose edge labels strictly increase along the path, and let f(n) be the minimum of l(lambda) over all such labelings. Determine the growth of f(n), in particular whether f(n) = o(n) and whether f(n) > n^(1/2 + epsilon) for some epsilon > 0.
accepted.context_brief: Increasing-label paths in edge-labeled complete graphs.

evidence.quote: Is f(n) = o(n)? Is f(n) > n^(1/2)+e for some e > 0?

accepted.question_text: Find a faster algorithm for computing the diameter of a graph than the matrix-multiplication-based bound cited in the source.
accepted.context_brief: Algorithmic complexity of graph diameter computation.

evidence.quote: Find a fast algorithm to determine the diameter of a graph.

accepted.question_text: For each integer k >= 1, is it true that every (2k - 1)-connected graph contains a spanning bipartite subgraph that is k-connected?
accepted.context_brief: Highly connected graphs with highly connected spanning bipartite subgraphs.

evidence.quote: Is it true that every (2k - 1)-connected graph has a k-connected spanning bipartite subgraph?
